[[New Conservatives Party]] (2019–2022) | profession = Company manager | spouse = | children = | alma_mater = | website = }} '''Cassandra Jane '''"'''Casey'''"''' Costello''' (born 1965 or 1966) is a New Zealand politician, lobbyist and former police officer. She was elected to the [[New Zealand House of Representatives]], representing the [[New Zealand First]] party, in the [[2023 New Zealand general election]]. She was appointed [[Minister of Customs (New Zealand)|Minister of Customs]], [[Minister for Seniors]] and Associate Minister of Health in the [[Sixth National Government of New Zealand]].{{Cite web |date=27 November 2023 |title=Who's in the new Cabinet? The full list of ministers |url= https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/who-are-the-new-cabinet-ministers-full-line-up-revealed-in-national-act-nz-first-government/B6XJTNCRFFFVNCY6SFZ7FHAKAI/ |access-date=27 November 2023 |website=NZ Herald |language=en-NZ}}{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Nicholas |date=24 November 2023 |title=Who are the new Cabinet ministers? Full list revealed in National-Act-NZ First Government |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/who-are-the-new-cabinet-ministers-full-line-up-revealed-in-national-act-nz-first-government/B6XJTNCRFFFVNCY6SFZ7FHAKAI/ |access-date=1 February 2024 |website=New Zealand Herald}} ==Early life and career== Costello's parents are [[Horse racing|racing]] journalist John Costello and New Zealand tennis representative Maryann Davis.{{Cite web |date=11 November 2023 |title='Most Māori are successful' – Casey Costello pushes message of aspiration |url= https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/casey-costello-what-drives-nz-first-new-mp-and-port-waikato-byelection-candidate/COQORARWORAE7PVYDEFS3TY5RQ/ |access-date=10 November 2023 |website=NZ Herald |language=en-NZ}} She is one of six children. She is of [[Māori people|Māori]], [[Scotland|Scottish]] and [[Ireland|Irish]] descent.{{cite web |last=Mays |first=Richard |date=7 May 2018 |title=Forum to be held on Māori wards |url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/manawatu-standard/news/103513430/forum-to-be-held-on-mori-wards |access-date=19 September 2023 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]}}{{Cite news |date=18 September 2023 |title=Costello rockets up NZ First list |language=en-NZ |website=Waatea News: Māori Radio Station |url= https://waateanews.com/2023/09/18/costello-rockets-up-nz-first-list/ |access-date=16 October 2023}} Her father's ancestors were British settlers who arrived in New Zealand in 1860.{{Cite web |date=11 November 2023 |title=Casey Costello: First I am a New Zealander |url= https://www.nzherald.co.nz/northland-age/news/casey-costello-first-i-am-a-new-zealander/SLZ7KBXLV7TLPQPKRAJE4UK7PA/ |access-date=10 November 2023 |website=NZ Herald |language=en-NZ}} Her iwi affiliations, through her mother, are [[Ngātiwai]], [[Ngāti Hau]] and [[Ngāpuhi]]; she is a relative of former politicians [[Kelvin Davis (politician)|Kelvin Davis]] and [[Hone Harawira]]. Costello's secondary schooling was at [[Marcellin College, Auckland]]. After leaving school, Costello worked in an ice cream parlour and also as a reporter with her father at the ''Counties Sport and News'' newspaper. In a 2023 interview, she stated that working as a crime reporter inspired her to join the [[New Zealand Police]], which she did in 1986. Her fourteen-year, Auckland-based policing career included working the 1992 [[Schlaepfer family murders]] and a period as vice-president of the police union, being the first woman elected to that role.{{Cite news |last=de Silva |first=Tommy |date=16 October 2023 |title=Meet the new NZ First MPs |language=en |work=The Spinoff |url= https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/16-10-2023/meet-the-new-nz-first-mps |access-date=16 October 2023}} She later became a security specialist and building services company manager in [[Auckland]]. In the 2000s, she was Parliament's manager of security and operations, overseeing a security upgrade. == Lobbyist career == From 2016, Costello was a founding trustee of [[Hobson's Pledge]] with former [[ACT New Zealand]] leader [[Don Brash]]. Hobson's Pledge is a right-wing [[lobby group]] that disputes some constitutional powers of the [[Treaty of Waitangi]] and aims to nullify the partnership between [[New Zealand Government|the Crown]] and Māori.{{Cite web |title=About us |url= https://www.hobsonspledge.nz/about_us |access-date=13 June 2022 |website=Hobson's Pledge}} Costello was a prominent spokesperson for the lobby group.{{Cite web |date=11 November 2023 |title='Your day is done': Conflict erupts at controversial Māori ward meeting |url= https://www.nzherald.co.nz/bay-of-plenty-times/news/war-of-words-tauranga-residents-butt-heads-at-controversial-maori-ward-meeting/5QAPDKYPSD7DWRVSFDQM7KR3UA/ |access-date=10 November 2023 |website=NZ Herald |language=en-NZ}}{{Cite web |date=19 June 2023 |title=Healthcare must be prioritised based on need, not race |url= https://waikanaewatch.org/2023/06/20/healthcare-must-be-prioritised-based-on-need-not-race/ |access-date=10 November 2023 |website=Waikanae Watch |language=en-US}}{{cite web |last=Bathgate |first=Benn |date=27 June 2017 |title=Treaty tussle follows meet of Hobson's Pledge |url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/94116037/treaty-tussle-follows-meet-of-hobsons-pledge |access-date=19 September 2023 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]}} Costello's view is that any policies seeking to redress [[Treaty of Waitangi claims and settlements|historical injustices against Māori]] are "racist and separatist." She campaigned against the creation of the Australian [[Indigenous Voice to Parliament]] at the [[2023 Australian Indigenous Voice referendum|2023 referendum]], writing in ''[[The Spectator|The Spectator Australia]]'' that New Zealand's equivalent to the Voice had "divided" New Zealanders.{{Cite web |date=19 April 2023 |title=New Zealand's Voice divided us |url= https://www.spectator.com.au/2023/04/new-zealands-voice-divided-us/ |access-date=10 November 2023 |website=The Spectator Australia |language=en-US}} Costello has also been involved in the [[New Zealand Taxpayers' Union]], a right-wing lobby group, including as board chair.{{Cite news |last=McConnell |first=Glenn |date=15 October 2023 |title=Who's coming and going in Parliament after seismic election result |language=en |work=Stuff |url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/133123170/whos-coming-and-going-in-parliament-after-seismic-election-result |access-date=16 October 2023}} She resigned from the board so that she could stand in the 2023 general election.{{cite news |last1=Williams |first1=David |title=Chiding in plain sight |url=https://newsroom.co.nz/2023/10/31/chiding-in-plain-sight/ |access-date=24 December 2023 |work=[[Newsroom (website)|Newsroom]] |date=31 October 2023}} Costello is also a trustee of the Migrant Exploitation Relief Foundation, pushing for investigation of the exploitation of illegal immigrants.{{Cite web |last=Du Plessis-Allan |first=Heather |date=25 September 2023 |title='Tragic workforce underbelly': Migrant Exploitation Relief Foundation trustee calls for further investigation |url= https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/on-air/heather-du-plessis-allan-drive/audio/casey-costello-migrant-exploitation-relief-foundation-trustee-on-overstayers-living-in-a-west-auckland-backyard-shanty-town/ |access-date=16 October 2023 |website=Newstalk ZB |language=en-nz}} ==Political career== {{NZ parlbox header|align=left}} {{NZ parlbox|term=54th|start={{NZ election link year|2023}}|end=present|list=3|party=New Zealand First|electorate=List}} {{End}} ===Early political career=== Costello first stood for parliament in 2011. Her brother, Dominic Costello, was the [[ACT New Zealand]] candidate in [[Te Atatū (New Zealand electorate)|Te Atatū]] in the [[2011 New Zealand general election|2011 general election]] and encouraged her to stand for the party also. She contested the [[Māngere (New Zealand electorate)|Māngere electorate]] and was ranked 34th on the [[Party lists in the 2011 New Zealand general election#ACT New Zealand|party list]],{{cite web |title=Party lists from the 2011 General Election |url= https://elections.nz/democracy-in-nz/historical-events/2011-general-election/party-lists-from-the-2011-general-election/ |access-date=23 August 2024 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}} but was not elected.{{cite web |title=Official Count Results – Māngere |url= http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2011/electorate-22.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=10 September 2013}} In 2019, Costello was involved with the [[New Conservatives Party]]. She joined the party's board at the beginning of 2019, as did [[David Moffett]].{{Cite press release |date=24 January 2019| title=New Conservative – from Strength to Strength |publisher=New Conservative |url= https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1901/S00106/new-conservative-from-strength-to-strength.htm |access-date=17 December 2023 |agency=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] }}{{Cite news |date=28 January 2019 |title=Hobson's Pledge leads Costello to New Conservatism |language=en-NZ |work=Waatea News |url= https://waateanews.com/2019/01/28/hobsons-pledge-leads-costello-to-new-conservatism/ |access-date=17 December 2023}}{{cite news |last1=Braae |first1=Alex |title='NZs resurgent New Conservatives: riding the culture wars to the 2020 election |url= https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/25-07-2019/nzs-resurgent-new-conservatives-riding-the-culture-wars-to-the-2020-election |access-date=23 December 2023 |work=[[The Spinoff]] |date=25 July 2019}} ===2023 general election=== Three years later, Costello later shifted her party affiliation and was selected by [[New Zealand First]] to contest the {{NZ electorate link|Port Waikato}} electorate at the {{NZ election link|2023}}.{{cite press release |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230723094032/https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2307/S00119/new-zealand-first-announces-casey-costello-as-candidate-for-2023-election.htm |archive-date=23 July 2023 |date=22 July 2023 |title=New Zealand First Announces Casey Costello As Candidate For 2023 Election |url= https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2307/S00119/new-zealand-first-announces-casey-costello-as-candidate-for-2023-election.htm |publisher=New Zealand First Party |agency=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] }} She was ranked third on the [[party list]].{{cite web |date=16 September 2023 |title=Election 2023: New Zealand First releases party list |url= https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/498125/election-2023-new-zealand-first-releases-party-list |work=[[Radio New Zealand]]}} At the New Zealand First conference where her candidacy was announced, Costello submitted a proposal that it should be party policy to remove the “exclusive authority of the Waitangi Tribunal to determine the meaning and effect” of the Treaty of Waitangi, along with other suggested changes to the Tribunal's authority.{{Cite news |author=Adam Pearse |date=16 October 2023 |title=NZ First members vote to scrap Waitangi Tribunal, build gang-only prison |language=en-NZ |work=NZ Herald |url= https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/nz-first-conference-party-members-vote-to-scrap-waitangi-tribunal-build-gang-only-prison/2Q2GUPAKDJCIHJIS4OZL5OTJZE/ |access-date=16 October 2023}} The proposal was approved, with the support of senior New Zealand First figures [[Winston Peters]] and [[Shane Jones]]. Costello also identified the removal of the [[Māori Health Authority]] as one of the first things she would like to accomplish if elected. Costello was elected to parliament as a list MP on 14 October 2023, based on New Zealand First's 6.08% share of the party vote.{{cite web |title=2023 General Election: Successful candidates |url= https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/successful-candidates.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=20 November 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20231117114239/https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/successful-candidates.html |archive-date=17 November 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}}{{cite web |title=Official count – Overall Results |url= https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/ |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=20 November 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20231107112928/https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/ |archive-date=7 November 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}} The electorate vote in Port Waikato was cancelled on 9 October 2023 after ACT candidate Neil Christensen died. Costello was automatically renominated for the [[2023 Port Waikato by-election|Port Waikato by-election]] held on 25 November 2023.{{cite news |last=Ensor |first=Jamie |date=10 October 2023 |title=Port Waikato by-election: Prime Minister Chris Hipkins announces date after ACT candidate dies |publisher=Newshub |url= https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/10/port-waikato-by-election-prime-minister-chris-hipkins-announces-date-after-act-candidate-dies.html|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20231010051025/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/10/port-waikato-by-election-prime-minister-chris-hipkins-announces-date-after-act-candidate-dies.html|url-status= dead|archive-date= 10 October 2023}} Costello came second place in the by-election, gaining 2,864 votes.{{cite web |title=Port Waikato – Official Result |url= https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/2023_port_waikato_byelection/index.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |date=6 December 2023|access-date=7 December 2023|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20231207202840/https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/2023_port_waikato_byelection/index.html|archive-date=7 December 2023|url-status=live}} ===First term, 2023–present=== New Zealand First formed a [[Sixth National Government of New Zealand|coalition government]] with the [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]] and ACT New Zealand. In late November 2023, Costello was appointed [[Minister of Customs (New Zealand)|Minister of Customs]], [[Minister for Seniors]], and an associate minister in the health, immigration and police portfolios in the coalition government.{{cite news |title=Cabinet lineup for new government unveiled – who gets what? |url= https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503156/cabinet-lineup-for-new-government-unveiled-who-gets-what |access-date=15 December 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=24 November 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20231204122806/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503156/cabinet-lineup-for-new-government-unveiled-who-gets-what |archive-date=4 December 2023|url-status=live}} ====Associate health==== As Associate Minister of Health, Costello is responsible for the government's policies on tobacco smoking,{{Cite news |last=Hauiti |first=Claudette |date=13 December 2023 |title=Smokefree roll back delegated to rookie minister |url=https://waateanews.com/2023/12/13/smokefree-roll-back-delegated-to-rookie-minister/ |access-date=24 January 2024 |website=[[Radio Waatea|Waatea News]] |language=en-NZ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240126064659/https://waateanews.com/2023/12/13/smokefree-roll-back-delegated-to-rookie-minister/|archive-date=26 January 2024|url-status=live}} including the proposed repeal of the [[Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products (Smoked Tobacco) Amendment Act 2022]], which would have restricted tobacco sales.{{Cite news|last=Espiner|first=Guyon|date=25 January 2024 |title=Official documents suggest a NZ First minister wants to freeze excise tax on cigarettes - but she denies it |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/in-depth/507471/official-documents-suggest-a-nz-first-minister-wants-to-freeze-excise-tax-on-cigarettes-but-she-denies-it |access-date=24 January 2024 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |language=en-nz |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240124190128/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/in-depth/507471/official-documents-suggest-a-nz-first-minister-wants-to-freeze-excise-tax-on-cigarettes-but-she-denies-it|archive-date=24 January 2024|url-status=live}} On 25 January 2024, [[Radio New Zealand]] (RNZ) reported that Costello had proposed a three year freeze on Consumer Price Index-related excise increases for smoked tobacco and removing the excise tax from smokeless tobacco products. Costello has denied having any links to the tobacco industry. Costello also proposed harsher penalties for selling [[vaping]] products to minors, including a NZ$30,000 fine for selling vapes to minors. Costello has disagreed with a [[prohibition]] on tobacco, instead advocating the decriminalisation of oral nicotine products such as snus and chewing tobacco. Costello's proposed three-year tobacco tax freeze was criticised by [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour]]'s health spokesperson [[Ayesha Verrall]] and anti-smoking advocates [[Health Coalition Aotearoa]] co-chairperson Boyd Swinburn, [[Asthma and Respiratory Foundation NZ]] chief executive Letitia Harding, [[Health Aotearoa Commission]] co-chairperson Leitu Tufuga, and [[Action on Smoking and Health]] (ASH) director Ben Youden as detrimental to efforts to combat smoking and improve public health.{{cite news |last1=Dunn |first1=Jordan |title=Call for Casey Costello to be removed after 'outrageous' proposal for tax freeze on tobacco |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/507554/call-for-casey-costello-to-be-removed-after-outrageous-proposal-for-tax-freeze-on-tobacco |access-date=26 January 2024 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=25 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240126070545/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/507554/call-for-casey-costello-to-be-removed-after-outrageous-proposal-for-tax-freeze-on-tobacco |archive-date=26 January 2024|url-status=live}} In response to criticism, [[Minister of Health (New Zealand)|Health Minister]] [[Shane Reti]] expressed confidence in Costello's role as Associate Health Minister and reaffirmed the Government's commitment to reducing smoking rates and tobacco consumption.{{cite news |last1=Witton |first1=Birdie |title=NZ First MP under fire over cigarette pricing document leak |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/350157980/nz-first-mp-casey-costello-under-fire-over-cigarette-pricing-document-leak |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=25 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240125045017/https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/350157980/nz-first-mp-casey-costello-under-fire-over-cigarette-pricing-document-leak |archive-date=25 January 2024|url-status=live}} Luxon subsequently stated that Costello was only exploring smoking policy health options and has made a mistake during an interview. He also expressed confidence in Costello and confirmed that the Government would not pause increases to the tobacco tax.{{cite news |title=Casey Costello tobacco excise possibly a mistake - PM Christopher Luxon |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/507909/casey-costello-tobacco-excise-possibly-a-mistake-pm-christopher-luxon |access-date=29 January 2024 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=30 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240129212532/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/507909/casey-costello-tobacco-excise-possibly-a-mistake-pm-christopher-luxon |archive-date=29 January 2024|url-status=live}} However, notes that Costello sent to health officials on reforming smoke free laws make it clear that a proposed freeze on excise tax for tobacco came from her office. The notes made the case that the tobacco industry is in real financial trouble, claiming "The tobacco industry in New Zealand is on its knees" and comparing the harm from nicotine to the harm from coffee, claiming "Nicotine is as harmful as caffeine.{{Cite news|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/in-depth/508127/revealed-nz-first-minister-casey-costello-s-notes-on-tobacco-tax-freeze|title=Revealed: NZ First Minister Casey Costello's notes on tobacco tax freeze|publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]]|date=1 February 2024|first=Guy|last=Espiner}}{{Cite news|last=Espiner |first=Guyon |date=2 February 2024 |title=Smokefree laws: Obtained notes show NZ First Minister Casey Costello's specific request on tobacco tax freeze |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/02/smokefree-laws-obtained-notes-show-nz-first-minister-casey-costello-s-specific-request-on-tobacco-tax-freeze.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240201044003/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/02/smokefree-laws-obtained-notes-show-nz-first-minister-casey-costello-s-specific-request-on-tobacco-tax-freeze.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=1 February 2024 |access-date=2 February 2024 |work=[[Newshub]]}} On 27 February 2024, Costello confirmed that the Government would introduce the Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products Amendment Bill under urgency to repeal the three components of the Smokefree legislation: the retail reduction scheme, de-nicotisation and the smokefree generation measures.{{cite web |title=Smokefree Amendment Bill introduced |url=https://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/smokefree-amendment-bill-introduced |website=Beehive.govt.nz |publisher=[[New Zealand Government]] |access-date=1 March 2024 |date=27 February 2024 |url-status=live |archive-date=29 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229120329/https://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/smokefree-amendment-bill-introduced }} The Smokefree Amendment Bill passed its third reading on 28 February 2024. During the first reading, Costello described Labour's Smokefree policy as an "untested regime" focusing on prohibition and said the Government wanted a "practical, workable, and tested approach" to tobacco. She also claimed that vaping could help reduce tobacco addiction and reiterated the Government's commitment to combating smoking. Labour leader [[Chris Hipkins]] accused Costello of regurgitating the [[tobacco industry]]'s talking points.{{cite news |title=Smokefree generation law scrapped by coalition government |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/510439/smokefree-generation-law-scrapped-by-coalition-government |access-date=1 March 2024 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=28 February 2024 |archive-date=29 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229155751/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/510439/smokefree-generation-law-scrapped-by-coalition-government |url-status=live }} On 20 March 2024, Costello announced that the Government would introduce legislation to ban disposable vapes, and increase the maximum fine from selling to under-18s from $10,000 to $100,000.{{Cite news |title='Crackdown': Total ban on disposable vapes, retailer fines increase |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/03/20/crackdown-total-ban-on-disposable-vapes-retailer-fines-increase/ |access-date=20 March 2024 |date=20 March 2024 |work=[[1News]] |publisher=[[TVNZ]] |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240320093902/https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/03/20/crackdown-total-ban-on-disposable-vapes-retailer-fines-increase/|archive-date=20 March 2024|url-status=live}} On 11 July 2024, Costello was rebuked by the Chief Ombudsman Judge [[Peter Boshier]] and ordered to apologise to public broadcaster [[RNZ]] and [[University of Otago]] public health professor [[Janet Hoek]] for failing to provide them with [[Official Information Act 1982|Official Information Act]] (OIA) information about the Government's tobacco and vaping policies. Boshier said withholding the information was "unreasonable and contrary to law".{{cite news |last1=Espiner |first1=Guyon |title=NZ First Minister Casey Costello forced to apologise after acting 'contrary to law' |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/350338927/nz-first-minister-casey-costello-forced-apologise-after-acting-contrary-law |access-date=12 July 2024 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=11 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240711040344/https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/350338927/nz-first-minister-casey-costello-forced-apologise-after-acting-contrary-law |archive-date=11 July 2024|url-status=live}} On 18 July, Casey Costello slashed the excise rate on [[heated tobacco product]]s (HTPs) by 50 percent as part of a trial to reduce smoking rates. The [[Ministry of Health (New Zealand)|Ministry of Health]] expressed disagreement, stating "there is no evidence to support HTPs use as a quit smoking tool".{{Cite web |date=2024-07-18 |title=NZ First Minister Casey Costello orders 50% cut to excise tax on heated tobacco products |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/in-depth/522429/nz-first-minister-casey-costello-orders-50-percent-cut-to-excise-tax-on-heated-tobacco-products |access-date=2024-07-18 |website=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718062711/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/in-depth/522429/nz-first-minister-casey-costello-orders-50-percent-cut-to-excise-tax-on-heated-tobacco-products|archive-date=18 July 2024|url-status=live}}{{cite news |title=Watch: Minister Casey Costello says heated tobacco tax cuts a 'trial' |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/522466/watch-minister-casey-costello-says-heated-tobacco-tax-cuts-a-trial |access-date=21 July 2024 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=18 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718113353/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/522466/watch-minister-casey-costello-says-heated-tobacco-tax-cuts-a-trial |archive-date=18 July 2024}} On 19 September 2024, Costello was reprimanded again by the Chief Ombudsman Boshier for her handling of a mystery document containing tobacco-industry friendly ideas, which she passed to health officials to develop policy.{{cite news |last1=Espiner |first1=Guyon |title=Chief Ombudsman criticises Costello over withholding tobacco documents |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/528429/chief-ombudsman-criticises-costello-over-withholding-tobacco-documents |access-date=23 September 2024 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=19 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240922220624/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/528429/chief-ombudsman-criticises-costello-over-withholding-tobacco-documents |archive-date=22 September 2024|url-status=live}} On 3 October, Costello released five documents which constituted her "independent advice" on heated tobacco products. These documents did not support her premise that HTPs were an alternative to smoking.{{cite news |title=Casey Costello releases 'independent' advice on heated tobacco |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/529782/casey-costello-releases-independent-advice-on-heated-tobacco |access-date=28 October 2024 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=3 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009073602/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/529782/casey-costello-releases-independent-advice-on-heated-tobacco |archive-date=9 October 2024}} On 21 October 2024, Costello announced that ambulance provider [[Hato Hone St John]] would receive an additional NZ$21 million in government funding.{{cite news |title=Hato Hone St John to receive $21 million funding boost |url=https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/on-air/heather-du-plessis-allan-drive/audio/casey-costello-associate-health-minister-on-the-government-confirming-a-funding-boost-for-hato-hone-st-john/ |access-date=28 October 2024 |work=[[Newstalk ZB]] |date=23 October 2024}} On 24 October, the Ministry of Health apologised to Costello after failing to inform her that one of its officials advising her on tobacco reform was the sister-in-law of Labour's health spokesperson [[Ayesha Verrall]], which constituted a [[conflict of interest]]. NZ First leader [[Winston Peters]] and [[Prime Minister of New Zealand|Prime Minister]] [[Christopher Luxon]] criticised the Health Ministry for not following its protocols.{{cite news |last1=McCulloch |first1=Craig |title=Ministry of Health apologises to minister over failure to disclose conflict of interest |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/531809/ministry-of-health-apologises-to-minister-over-failure-to-disclose-conflict-of-interest |access-date=28 October 2024 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=24 October 2024}}{{cite news |last1=Ensor |first1=Jamie |title=Christopher Luxon calls out ministry for failing to tell Casey Costello worker was Ayesha Verrall's relative |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/christopher-luxon-calls-out-ministry-of-health-for-failing-to-tell-casey-costello-worker-was-ayesha-verralls-relative-chris-hipkins-admits-using-wrong-words/C6BQWQ6PCNEHLHYDAFUNRBY7KE/ |access-date=28 October 2024 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=25 October 2024}} As Associate Health Minister, Costello sponsored legislation in mid-December 2024 repealing the previous Labour Government's Therapeutic Products Act 2023, which would have increased regulatory oversight over therapeutic and medical products from 2026.{{cite press release |last1=Costello |first1=Casey |title=Therapeutic Products Act repeal bull passed |url=https://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/therapeutic-products-act-repeal-bill-passed |website=Beehive.govt.nz |publisher=[[New Zealand Government]] |access-date=11 March 2026 |date=13 December 2024 |url-status=live}} In mid April 2025, [[Radio New Zealand]] reported that Costello had directed [[Health New Zealand]] in late March 2025 to use "clear language" in its communications about health issues. Costello had stated: "Recent documents that have reached my office from the Ministry of Health have referred to women as 'pregnant people', 'people with a cervix' or 'individuals capable of childbearin' [sic]. Only women and people of the female sex can get pregnant and birth a child no matter how they identify."{{cite news |title=Coalition directs Health NZ to stop saying 'pregnant people' |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/558168/coalition-directs-health-nz-to-stop-saying-pregnant-people |access-date=15 April 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=27 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250415101400/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/558168/coalition-directs-health-nz-to-stop-saying-pregnant-people |archive-date=15 April 2025}} Costello's directive was criticised by [[Victoria University of Wellington]] senior lecturer George Parker and ''[[The Spinoff]]'' editor [[Madeleine Chapman]] for rolling back the use of "inclusive language" in official health communications.{{cite news |last1=Chapman |first1=Madeleine |title=A deeply frustrating line-by-line reading of Casey Costello's letter to Health NZ |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/15-04-2025/a-deeply-frustrating-line-by-line-reading-of-casey-costellos-letter-to-health-nz |access-date=15 April 2025 |work=[[The Spinoff]] |date=15 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250415212227/https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/15-04-2025/a-deeply-frustrating-line-by-line-reading-of-casey-costellos-letter-to-health-nz |archive-date=15 April 2025}} In November 2025, Costello defended New Zealand's sharp decline in the [https://globaltobaccoindex.org/gti/2025 Global Tobacco Industry Interference Index], which saw the country fall from second place in 2023 to 53rd. The report cited the government's repeal of the smokefree generation laws, a tax concession benefiting [[Philip Morris International|Philip Morris]], and the movement of staff between politics and lobbying as factors in the drop. Costello called the index "ridiculous" and “absolutely ludicrous," saying she had been transparent in all dealings and that the comparison with higher-smoking countries was "nonsense." She maintained that the country still had one of the world's lowest smoking rates and described the ''Smokefree 2025'' target as ambitious but achievable.{{Cite news |date=20 November 2025 |title='Absolutely ludicrous': Casey Costello defends plunge in global tobacco control ranking |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/579431/absolutely-ludicrous-casey-costello-defends-plunge-in-global-tobacco-control-ranking |access-date=20 November 2025 |work=RNZ}} ====Customs and associate immigration==== On 10 May 2025, Costello announced that the Government would allocate NZ$35 million from the [[2025 New Zealand budget]] into combating drug smuggling, improving supply chain security and expanding the [[New Zealand Customs Service]]'s overseas presence.{{cite news |title=Government puts $35m towards keeping drugs out of the country |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2025/05/10/government-puts-35m-towards-keeping-drugs-out-of-the-country/ |access-date=12 May 2025 |work=[[1News]] |publisher=[[TVNZ]] |ref=10 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250512050326/https://www.1news.co.nz/2025/05/10/government-puts-35m-towards-keeping-drugs-out-of-the-country/ |archive-date=12 May 2025 |url-status=live}} On 22 May 2026, Costello announced that the Government would allocate $70 million from the [[2026 New Zealand budget]] to purchasing three new [[unmanned underwater vehicle]]s (UUVs) for combating maritime smuggling. These UUVS will conduct checks below the waterline, reducing the need for diving crews.{{cite news |last1=Blackwell |first1=Finn |title=Customs unveils underwater tech to combat smugglers |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/top/596036/customs-unveils-underwater-tech-to-combat-smugglers |access-date=26 May 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=22 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260525173939/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/top/596036/customs-unveils-underwater-tech-to-combat-smugglers |archive-date=25 May 2026 |url-status=live}} On 24 June 2026, Costello announced that the [[Refugees in New Zealand#Community sponsorship|Community Organisation Refugee Sponsorship]] scheme would be made permanent from July 2026 and also expanded to 200 spaces per year from 2027.{{cite news |last1=McCulloch |first1=Craig |title=Government shifts more responsibility for refugees to community organisations |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/618815/government-shifts-more-responsibility-for-refugees-to-community-organisations |access-date=25 June 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=24 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260624024822/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/618815/government-shifts-more-responsibility-for-refugees-to-community-organisations |archive-date=24 June 2026 |url-status=live}} ====Associate police==== On 20 February 2025, Costello announced that the Government had appointed an Advisory Group to combat transnational and serious organised crime in New Zealand. She said that the Advisory Group would operate for eight months and be funded through the proceeds of crime fund. The Advisory Group consisted of Meredith Connell senior partner Steve Symon, Craig Hamilton, John Tims and [[Sociology|sociologist]] [[Jarrod Gilbert]].{{cite news |title=Advisory Group appointed to tackle organised crime groups |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/542500/advisory-group-appointed-to-tackle-organised-crime-groups |access-date=16 June 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=20 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250523012229/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/542500/advisory-group-appointed-to-tackle-organised-crime-groups |archive-date=23 May 2025 |url-status=live}} On 9 April, the Advisory Group released its first report to Costello, warning that New Zealand was vulnerable to the increased presence of organised crime groups from [[China]], [[Southeast Asia]], [[Latin America]] and [[Australia]] including New Zealand 501 deportees from Australia.{{cite news |title='Increasingly vulnerable' - Warning over rise of organised crime in NZ |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/557609/increasingly-vulnerable-warning-over-rise-of-organised-crime-in-nz |access-date=16 June 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=9 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250409232447/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/557609/increasingly-vulnerable-warning-over-rise-of-organised-crime-in-nz |archive-date=9 April 2025 |url-status=bot: unknown }} On 10 June, the Advisory Group released a third report warning that growing criminal networks in New Zealand made the country more vulnerable to corruption and "insider threats." In response, Costello expressed surprise that New Zealand was the only [[Five Eyes]] country to lack an anti-corruption strategy.{{cite news |title=Government warned corruption and 'insider threats' increasing in New Zealand |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/563587/government-warned-corruption-and-insider-threats-increasing-in-new-zealand |access-date=16 June 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=10 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250614042814/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/563587/government-warned-corruption-and-insider-threats-increasing-in-new-zealand |archive-date=14 June 2025 |url-status=live}} ==== Seniors ==== In May 2025, Labour spokesperson for Seniors Ingrid Leary accused Costello of being "missing in action" in her role as Minister for Seniors, citing responses to [[Official Information Act 1982|Official Information Act]] requests and written parliamentary questions showing that she had not taken any papers under the Seniors portfolio to Cabinet between late 2023 and March 2025. Leary also noted that Costello had issued only one press release in the role and argued that she had done more to support the tobacco industry than to advance the interests of older New Zealanders.{{Cite news |date=21 May 2025 |title=Labour's Ingrid Leary claims Casey Costello is not doing her job as Minister for Seniors |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/561631/labour-s-ingrid-leary-claims-casey-costello-is-not-doing-her-job-as-minister-for-seniors |access-date=20 November 2025 |work=RNZ}} Costello rejected the claims, saying they reflected a "shallow understanding" of the portfolio. She argued that the Office for Seniors is a small agency that does not typically generate Cabinet papers, and that much of the Seniors work programme involves cross-government coordination, including planning for aged-care improvements, changes enabling subsidiary dwellings, and the review of the Retirement Villages Act. Costello said older New Zealanders could be assured that all commitments to them in the NZ First–National coalition agreement would be delivered. In October 2025, Costello responded to the release of ''Care in Crisis'', a major NZ Nurses Organisation report based on interviews with aged-care workers that alleged widespread understaffing, missed care, and instances of neglect in residential aged-care facilities. The report described a sector "in crisis", citing inadequate staffing levels, delayed wound care, rationed incontinence products, rushed hygiene assistance, and unmet emotional and social needs. Costello disputed the findings, saying the accounts "paint a very distorted picture" and did not reflect the reality of most aged-care services. She argued the sector was not in crisis, highlighting $270 million in additional government funding over the preceding two years and stating that facilities she had visited were committed to high-quality care. Costello said broader reforms were underway, including work on a new system-level aged-care model and a forthcoming strategic vision for the sector.{{Cite news |date=13 October 2025 |title='Missed care and outright neglect': The 'crisis' in our aged care homes revealed |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/nz-news/360850116/missed-care-and-outright-neglect-crisis-our-aged-care-homes-revealed |access-date=20 November 2025 |work=Stuff}} ==Personal life== In mid-April 2025, Costello was verbally accosted by former [[Te Pāti Māori]] candidate Pere Huriwai-Seger at a [[Wellsford]] food court, who justified his actions by alleging that bullying was allowed to happen in Parliament. This incident followed an earlier incident in which fellow NZ First MP [[Shane Jones]]'s wife Dot Jones being allegedly assaulted at [[Auckland Airport]] and a report into increased harassment of female politicians.{{cite news |title=Hone Harawira criticises former Te Pāti Māori candidate Pere Huriwai-Seger for confronting Casey Costello |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/558457/hone-harawira-criticises-former-te-pati-maori-candidate-pere-huriwai-seger-for-confronting-casey-costello |access-date=21 April 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=17 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250421044341/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/558457/hone-harawira-criticises-former-te-pati-maori-candidate-pere-huriwai-seger-for-confronting-casey-costello |archive-date=21 April 2025 |url-status=live}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{subject bar|auto=y|d=y|Politics|New Zealand}} {{authority control}} {{Current members of the New Zealand House of Representatives}}{{New Zealand First}}{{Sixth National Government of New Zealand}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Costello, Casey}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Ngāpuhi people]] [[Category:New Zealand people of Scottish descent]] [[Category:New Zealand people of Irish descent]] [[Category:ACT New Zealand politicians]] [[Category:Unsuccessful candidates in the 2011 New Zealand general election]] [[Category:Candidates in the 2023 New Zealand general election]] [[Category:New Zealand First MPs]] [[Category:Members of the New Zealand House of Representatives]] [[Category:Women members of the New Zealand House of Representatives]] [[Category:Māori MPs]] [[Category:New Zealand list MPs]] [[Category:New Zealand police officers]] [[Category:Women government ministers of New Zealand]] [[Category:Government ministers of New Zealand]] [[Category:Ngāti Wai people]] [[Category:Ngāti Hau people]] [[Category:Year of birth missing (living people)]] [[Category:People educated at Marcellin College, Auckland]]
